name: scan-write-lock-on-the-fast-path
body: `cmd_scan` holds the per-checkout extended write lock (`artifacts::acquire_spec_lock`, a blocking `LOCK_EX` flock on `apg/.trans/specs.lock`) for the whole scan pipeline, including the freshness fast path where the tree is unchanged and the DB is reused with no frontend spawn and no rebuild — a read-only scan of an unchanged tree still takes an exclusive lock and can briefly block a staleness-gated reader. That is deliberate: the reuse decision and the rebuild stay under one lock, so a reader never judges a half-decided state. The same lock covers the previous-database read: after the fast-path return, `cmd_scan` takes exactly one read-only `PreviousScan::capture` before the pipeline discards or replaces `db.lbug`; the handle is released inside `capture`, so the rebuild replaces the database uncontended and no consumer opens a second handle on it. Upgrade trigger: if the fast path's brief exclusivity ever measurably delays a concurrent reader, acquire a shared (`LOCK_SH`) lock for the reusable branch only — do not weaken the exclusive hold on the discard-and-rebuild path or move the capture outside the lock.
